literal: Displaced people in every place had first been bullied by locals; hearing Gao had risen in revolt, they came to follow in masses—in a fortnight or so the host exceeded a hundred thousand.
idiomatic: Displaced people bullied by locals flocked to him when he rebelled; within a fortnight his host passed a hundred thousand.

literal: Before this the people of Henan often laughed at the people of Hebei for liking to eat elm leaves; therefore the people of Qi called them the Elm-Leaf Bandits.
idiomatic: Henan people had mocked Hebei folk for eating elm leaves, so Qi people called them the Elm-Leaf Bandits.

literal: Gao raided east into Guang Province, reached the sea and returned, and again defeated Commander Li Shuren's army.
idiomatic: Gao raided Guang Province to the sea and back, and again defeated Commander Li Shuren.

literal: An edict ordered Tianmu and Qi Shenwu to suppress him; they inflicted a great defeat.
idiomatic: Tianmu and Qi Shenwu were ordered to suppress him and won a great victory.

literal: Gao then asked to surrender; he was sent to the capital and beheaded.
idiomatic: Gao then surrendered, was sent to the capital, and beheaded.

literal: At the time Yuan Hao took advantage of the void and seized Xingyang.
idiomatic: Meanwhile Yuan Hao seized Xingyang while the realm was open.

literal: Hearing the emperor was touring north, Tianmu from Bigong ramparts crossed north and met the imperial carriage at Henei.
idiomatic: Hearing the emperor had gone north, Tianmu crossed from Bigong and met him at Henei.

literal: Erzhu Rong, because the season was hot, wished to withdraw the army.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, citing the heat, wished to withdraw.

literal: Tianmu firmly held that it could not be done; Rong then followed him.
idiomatic: Tianmu insisted they could not withdraw; Rong yielded.

literal: When the emperor returned to the palace, Tianmu was given Grand Preceptor, feathered canopy and martial pipes, and his fief increased to seventy thousand households in all.
idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Tianmu received Grand Preceptor, imperial insignia, and a fief of seventy thousand households.

literal: Tianmu, as a distant kinsman, originally had no virtue or fame; relying on the Erzhu clan, his rank at the time reached the utmost.
idiomatic: A distant kinsman without native renown, he rose to the summit on Erzhu patronage.

literal: His influence scorched court and countryside; dukes and marquises down filled his gate each morning;
idiomatic: His influence scorched court and countryside; nobles filled his gate each morning;

literal: he received bribes and treasures piled up.
idiomatic: bribes and treasures piled high.

literal: Yet he was lenient and accommodating and was not much resented at the time.
idiomatic: Yet he was lenient and not much resented.

literal: The emperor, because he was Rong's faction, outwardly showed favor; an edict allowed Tianmu's carriage and horses to pass through the Grand Marshal Gate.
idiomatic: The emperor outwardly favored him as Rong's ally and allowed his carriage through the Grand Marshal Gate.

literal: Tianmu and Rong relied on each other; Rong's faction treated him with elder-brother ritual.
idiomatic: He and Rong relied on each other; Rong's men treated him as elder brother.

literal: Though Shilong and others were Rong's sons and nephews and already held heavy rank, when Tianmu spoke of their faults Rong at once had them beaten—such was their intimacy and trust.
idiomatic: Even Rong's nephews, though exalted, were beaten when Tianmu reported their faults—such was Rong's trust.

literal: The emperor inwardly feared and hated him; he was killed together with Rong.
idiomatic: The emperor inwardly feared him; he was killed with Rong.

literal: At the beginning of Jiemin he was posthumously made Chancellor, Grand General of the Pillar of State, Governor of Yong Province, with the Golden Axe by commission, posthumous name Wuzhao.
idiomatic: Under Jiemin he was posthumously Chancellor, Grand General of the Pillar of State, Governor of Yong, with the Golden Axe, posthumous name Wuzhao.

literal: His son Yan inherited; handsome talent and appearance; held the post of Director of the Bureau of Justice.
idiomatic: His son Yan inherited—handsome and talented—and served as Director of the Bureau of Justice.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, hearing the summons to court, he feigned illness and died of terror.
idiomatic: When Qi took the mandate, summoned to court he feigned illness and died of fear.

literal: Duke of Xihe Dun was a great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.
idiomatic: Duke of Xihe Dun was a great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.

literal: At the beginning of Daowu he followed campaigns; his name topped the generals.
idiomatic: At the start of Daowu he campaigned; his name stood first among generals.

literal: Later he followed the campaign on Zhongshan; wherever he went none stood before him.
idiomatic: Later in the Zhongshan campaign he swept all before him.

literal: Under Mingyuan he was appointed Grand Officer of the Central Court.
idiomatic: Under Mingyuan he was Grand Officer of the Central Court.

literal: Under Taiwu he was advanced to Duke of Xihe; favor grew ever deeper.
idiomatic: Under Taiwu he was advanced to Duke of Xihe and favored ever more deeply.

literal: He died; his son Bo inherited.
idiomatic: He died; his son Bo inherited.

literal: Minister of Works Shi was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.
idiomatic: Minister of Works Shi was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Pingwen.

literal: He had daring and strategy.
idiomatic: He had daring and strategy.

literal: He followed Taiwu's southern campaign to Guabu Mountain.
idiomatic: He followed Taiwu's southern campaign as far as Guabu Mountain.

literal: He held Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yong Province, and successively served as Vice Director of the Northern Department and Governor of Hua Province.
idiomatic: He served as Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yong, and also as Vice Director of the Northern Department and Governor of Hua.

literal: Prince of Wuwei Wei was the fourth son of Emperor Lie.
idiomatic: Prince of Wuwei Wei was the fourth son of Emperor Lie.

literal: Broad and elegant, with general's strategy.
idiomatic: Broad and elegant, he possessed a commander's strategy.

literal: He often followed Daowu in campaigns with merit and was appointed General of the Martial Guard.
idiomatic: He often followed Daowu in campaigns with merit and was made General of the Martial Guard.

literal: His son Wuzhen had strength beyond others; following Daowu in conquest he had repeated battle merit and reached Governor of Julu.
idiomatic: His son Wuzhen's strength was unmatched; he followed Daowu in conquest, won repeated honors, and became Governor of Julu.

literal: His son Xingdu was clever, keen, and resolute.
idiomatic: His son Xingdu was clever, keen, and resolute.

literal: Under Wencheng he was Governor of Hejian and enfeoffed Viscount of Lecheng.
idiomatic: Under Wencheng he governed Hejian and was enfeoffed Viscount of Lecheng.

literal: His government was stern and fierce; the people feared him.
idiomatic: His rule was stern and fierce; the people feared him.

literal: At the beginning of Xianwen, because his son Pi was exalted, he was advanced to Marquis of Lecheng.
idiomatic: At the start of Xianwen, because his son Pi was exalted, he was advanced to Marquis of Lecheng.

literal: He resigned old age and returned home; the emperor treated him with increased ritual, gave couch, staff, and garments, and sent meals to his residence.
idiomatic: He retired in old age; the emperor honored him with couch, staff, garments, and meals sent to his home.

literal: His wife the Lady Lou was Grand Consort of Prince of Dongyang.
idiomatic: His wife Lady Lou was Grand Consort of the Prince of Dongyang.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Hejian, posthumous name Xuan.
idiomatic: He died, was posthumously Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Hejian, posthumous name Xuan.

literal: His son Ti inherited the ducal and marquisal titles.
idiomatic: His son Ti inherited the ducal and marquisal titles.

literal: Ti's younger brother Pi, under Taiwu followed the entourage to the Yangtze and was enfeoffed Viscount of Xingping.
idiomatic: Ti's younger brother Pi followed Taiwu to the Yangtze and was enfeoffed Viscount of Xingping.

literal: When Xianwen succeeded he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: When Xianwen took the throne he rose to Palace Attendant.

literal: Chancellor Yichun plotted rebellion; Pi reported it and an edict seized and executed Yichun.
idiomatic: Chancellor Yichun plotted rebellion; Pi reported it and Yichun was seized and executed.

literal: He was moved to Director of the Masters of Writing and changed to Duke of Dongyang.
idiomatic: He became Director of the Masters of Writing and was changed to Duke of Dongyang.

literal: Under Xiaowen he was made Prince of Dongyang, Palace Attendant, and Duke of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Under Xiaowen he was Prince of Dongyang, Palace Attendant, and nominal Duke of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When Pi's son Chao was born the imperial carriage personally visited his residence.
idiomatic: When Pi's son Chao was born the emperor visited his home in person.

literal: Because his loyalty was undivided, an edict granted Pi entry into the Eight Discussions, transmitted to descendants; offenses up to a hundred might be counted and forgiven.
idiomatic: For undivided loyalty an edict granted Pi the Eight Discussions for his line; offenses up to a hundred might be tallied and forgiven.

literal: His registered clansmen and corvée levies were released from mixed labor and tax, with request for restoration.
idiomatic: Registered clansmen and corvée levies were released from mixed labor and tax.

literal: If there were treacherous men who by convenience slandered him, they were at once beheaded.
idiomatic: Anyone who slandered him by treacherous means was to be beheaded at once.

literal: Soon he was moved to Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Soon he was Grand Preceptor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At the time Prince of Huainan Tuo, Prince of Huaiyang Yuanyuan, and Prince of Hedong Gougui were all honored as elders of former days.
idiomatic: Prince of Huainan Tuo, Prince of Huaiyang Yuanyuan, and Prince of Hedong Gougui were all honored as elders.

literal: Whenever there was a great affair they were brought into the inner palace; riding the step carriage with canes at court, they advanced and retreated together.
idiomatic: For great affairs they were brought within the palace, riding the step carriage with canes and moving as one at court.

literal: Pi, Tuo, and Yuanyuan were all stout in form, belts ten arm-spans, large ears and fine brows, beards and temples grizzled—the hundred offices watching were all awed.
idiomatic: Pi, Tuo, and Yuanyuan were all imposing—ten-span belts, large ears, fine brows, grizzled beards—and the court stood in awe.

literal: Only Gougui was somewhat short and inferior; his bearing also did not match them.
idiomatic: Only Gougui was shorter and less imposing.

literal: Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming honored age and revered the old, inquiring after them with full courtesy.
idiomatic: Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming honored age and treated the old with full courtesy.

literal: Pi's voice was high and clear; he broadly remembered state affairs;
idiomatic: Pi's voice rang clear; he remembered state affairs in detail;

literal: at banquets he always sat at the head;
idiomatic: at banquets he always sat at the head;

literal: he always spoke loudly, narrating past successes and failures; emperor and empress respectfully received it.
idiomatic: he spoke loudly of past successes and failures, and emperor and empress listened with respect.

literal: Yet he fawned on powerful men and insulted the lowly; whenever he saw Wang Rui or Fu Chengzu he would bend low.
idiomatic: Yet he fawned on the powerful and insulted the low; before Wang Rui or Fu Chengzu he bent low.

literal: At the time Empress Dowager Wenming built a mansion for Wang Rui; therefore one was also built for Pi.
idiomatic: When the empress dowager built a mansion for Wang Rui, one was built for Pi as well.

literal: When the mansion was finished, emperor and empress visited it and led the hundred civil and military officials in feast.
idiomatic: When it was finished the emperor and empress feasted there with the whole court.

literal: They had Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Rui proclaim the edict and bestow on Pi one gold seal.
idiomatic: Wang Rui proclaimed the edict and bestowed one gold seal on Pi.

literal: The empress dowager personally composed admonitory song-words and gave them to the officials; Pi memorialized thanks.
idiomatic: The empress dowager composed admonitory songs for the officials; Pi memorialized his thanks.

literal: The empress dowager ordered, "Ministers! Neighbors!"
idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Ministers—and neighbors!"

literal: "Neighbors! Ministers!"
idiomatic: "Neighbors—and ministers!"

literal: The ruler then has no dissipation above; ministers then tread ice below.
idiomatic: If the ruler does not dissipate above and ministers tread ice below,

literal: If it can be thus, is great peace hard to attain!"
idiomatic: great peace is not hard to attain!"

literal: When Pi's wife the Lady Duan died, posthumous name Consort Gong; he was also specially given gold tallies.
idiomatic: When Lady Duan died she received posthumous name Consort Gong; Pi was also given gold tallies.

literal: Later by precedent princely titles were reduced; he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyang commandery.
idiomatic: Later, by precedent, princely titles were reduced and he became Duke of Pingyang commandery.

literal: He asked to retire; the edict did not permit.
idiomatic: He asked to retire; the edict refused.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Pi and Prince of Guangling Yu remained to guard the capital, both with ceremonial staffs by commission.
idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Pi and Prince of Guangling Yu guarded the capital, both with ceremonial staffs.

literal: The edict to Pi and Yu said, "To remain on guard none but the worthy will do."
idiomatic: The edict said to Pi and Yu, "Only the worthy should guard the capital."

literal: The Grand Preceptor is advanced in years and heavy in virtue, his rank summing the balance-scale.
idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor is aged and weighty in virtue, his rank summing the realm's balance.

literal: Yu is Our beloved younger brother, gentle, bright, and decisive.
idiomatic: Yu is Our beloved brother—gentle, bright, and decisive.

literal: Therefore these two are left to guard the capital, given two staffs, reward and punishment in hand.
idiomatic: Therefore they guard the capital with two staffs and power over reward and punishment.

literal: Reverently fulfill the established statutes to match Our heart."
idiomatic: Fulfill the statutes faithfully to match Our intent."

literal: Pi replied, "I respectfully obey unto death."
idiomatic: Pi replied, "I will obey unto death."

literal: Yu replied, "The Grand Preceptor should alone hold command; I can only be second."
idiomatic: Yu replied, "The Grand Preceptor should command alone; I am only his deputy."

literal: The emperor said, "The old have wisdom, the young have decision—how can you decline?"
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wisdom in age, decision in youth—how can you refuse?"

literal: When the emperor returned to Dai, Pi asked to compose a song and the edict permitted it.
idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Dai, Pi asked to compose a song and was permitted.

literal: When the song ended the emperor said, "You urged Us to return the carriage, therefore We personally sing to state Our intent."
idiomatic: When the song ended the emperor said, "You urged Our return; We sing now to state Our intent."

literal: Now the construction already has its stages; therefore We temporarily return to the old capital, hoping later We may share this joy again."
idiomatic: Construction has its stages; We return temporarily to the old capital, hoping to share this joy again."

literal: Thereupon he ordered Pi and the others on the matter of moving the capital to each state his will.
idiomatic: He then ordered Pi and the others each to state his will on moving the capital.

literal: Governor of Yanzhou Mu Pi advanced and said, "The four quarters are not yet pacified—it is said the move should not be made."
idiomatic: Governor of Yanzhou Mu Pi said, "The realm is not yet pacified—the move should wait."

literal: I hear the Yellow Emperor dwelt at Zhuolu; ancient sage kings need not all dwell in the Central Plains."
idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor dwelt at Zhuolu; sage kings need not all live in the Central Plains."

literal: The emperor said, "The Yellow Emperor, because the realm was not settled, therefore dwelt at Zhuolu."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Yellow Emperor dwelt at Zhuolu because the realm was unsettled."

literal: Once settled, he also moved to Henan."
idiomatic: Once it was settled, he moved to Henan."

literal: Prince of Guangling Yu said, "I think to follow the divine rule and glorify the great enterprise—please decide it by divination."
idiomatic: Prince of Guangling Yu said, "Let us glorify the enterprise—please decide by divination."

literal: The emperor said, "Formerly Xuanyuan sought divination; the tortoise scorched—he asked Heaven's Elder, who said it was auspicious, and followed; in the end he attained prosperity."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Xuanyuan once divined; the tortoise scorched, Heaven's Elder called it auspicious, and prosperity followed."

literal: Then the utmost man's measure is not yet fixed; he is clearer than the tortoise.
idiomatic: The sage's measure is not yet fixed; he is clearer than the tortoise.

literal: The emperor again addressed the ministers, "Formerly Emperor Pingwen passed away and Zhaocheng established residence at Shengle."
idiomatic: He addressed the ministers again: "Pingwen passed away; Zhaocheng made Shengle his seat."

literal: Daowu, divinely martial, responded to Heaven and moved residence to Pingcheng.
idiomatic: Daowu, divinely martial, answered Heaven and moved to Pingcheng.

literal: We have fortunately inherited an age that overcame cruelty; therefore We move the dwelling to the Central Plains.
idiomatic: We inherit an age that overcame cruelty; therefore We move to the Central Plains.

literal: Northerners, within ten years, shall be allowed to move slowly.
idiomatic: Northerners may move slowly over ten years.

literal: We Ourselves have stored grain in abundance so they shall not suffer want.
idiomatic: We have stored grain abundantly so they shall not suffer want.

literal: Former Governor of Huaizhou Qinglong, former Governor of Qinzhou Lü Shou'en, and others still held stubborn folly; the emperor soothed and answered each; their words failed and they withdrew.
idiomatic: Former governors Qinglong and Lü Shou'en still argued stubbornly; the emperor answered each gently until they withdrew, defeated in argument.

literal: The emperor was again about to tour north; Pi was moved to Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing and repeatedly memorialized firm refusal.
idiomatic: When the emperor prepared to tour north again, Pi was made Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing and repeatedly refused the posts.
